interactions.summary: Carol reads Dante's invocation to Apollo, Minerva, and the Muses, and Jiang explains that the poet is summoning every available source of inspiration because this voyage is unprecedented.
The reading moves from Jason and the Argonauts to a thirst for the godly realm, and Jiang interprets that movement as Dante's claim that human beings are fundamentally hungry to return to God.
Carol reads Dante and Beatrice arriving with extreme suddenness at the first celestial sphere and being told to direct the mind gratefully toward God.

claims.claim: Jiang interprets Dante's appeal to Minerva, Apollo, and the Muses as an invocation of every possible form of inspiration needed for a journey no one has previously made.
Jiang says Dante's voyage is singular enough that no one else has been on it before and no one else will ever be on it again.
Jiang interprets the canto's language of thirst as evidence that the deepest human hunger is to return to God.
Jiang says Dante's increasing speed reflects the nearness of God, so movement toward the divine accelerates as desire and destination align.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang presents Dante's ascent as a once-only voyage requiring total inspiration because it traverses territory no one else can simply repeat.
signature_moments.source_phrase: No one's ever been on this journey before. And quite honestly, no one else will ever be on this journey again.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It raises the stakes of the canto from a generic religious poem to an unmatched visionary event.

signature_moments.moment: The poem's thirst for the godly realm becomes Jiang's anthropology of desire: the human creature is built to hunger for return.
signature_moments.source_phrase: our fundamental hunger, our fundamental need, our thirst, is to return to God
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is one of the packet's most reusable formulations for Dante's understanding of longing.

signature_moments.moment: The ascent is imaged as almost instantaneous flight, compressed into the time an arrow takes to leap and strike.
signature_moments.source_phrase: in a span perhaps no longer than an arrow takes
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The image makes Paradise feel governed by a speed of desire and grace unlike earthly motion.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Dante's phrase for the spiritual nourishment sought by the few readers able to follow him into Paradise.
The language Jiang turns into a general model of human desire as longing for return to God.

chronology_notes.note: After clarifying his method in the previous packet, Jiang now applies it directly to the canto: invocation, mythic comparison, desire, and velocity are all read as parts of a single model of ascent toward God.
